chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Fill in the blank and rewrite the completed statement: ____________ is the largest gland in the body.
solution: Liver is the largest gland in the body. The liver secretes bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the small intestine, where it emulsifies fats and makes the medium alkaline so that the pancreatic and intestinal enzymes can act on the food.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Find the odd one out and write it: vagina, uterus, vas deferens, ovary.
solution: Odd one out: vas deferens. The vas deferens is a duct of the MALE reproductive system (it carries sperms from the epididymis of the testis towards the urethra), whereas the vagina, uterus and ovary are all organs of the FEMALE reproductive system.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false: Aquatic animals breathe at a slower rate than the terrestrial animals.
solution: False. Aquatic animals breathe at a FASTER rate than terrestrial animals. The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is far less than the oxygen available in air, so an aquatic animal has to pass a much larger volume of water over its respiratory surface (gills) to obtain the same amount of oxygen. Hence its rate of breathing is faster than that of a terrestrial animal.

stem: Considering the relationship in the first pair, complete the second pair: rr : Homozygous : : Rr : ____________
solution: rr : Homozygous : : Rr : Heterozygous. In the genotype 'rr' both the alleles of the gene are identical, so the individual is homozygous (pure) for that character. In 'Rr' the two alleles are different — one dominant (R) and one recessive (r) — so the individual is heterozygous (hybrid).

stem: Name the following: Main ore of aluminium.
solution: Bauxite, \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot 2H_2O}\) (hydrated aluminium oxide), is the main ore of aluminium. The bauxite is first purified to alumina \(\mathrm{(Al_2O_3)}\) by the Bayer process, and the alumina is then reduced electrolytically to obtain aluminium metal.

stem: ____________ liberated when acetic acid reacts with sodium metal.
solution: Hydrogen. Acetic acid (ethanoic acid) is a carboxylic acid, and like other acids it reacts with an active metal such as sodium to give the corresponding salt together with hydrogen gas, which is liberated with brisk effervescence: \(\mathrm{2CH_3COOH + 2Na \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2 \uparrow}\). (Sodium acetate is the salt formed.)

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: For binary fission, Amoeba required ____________ parent cells.
solution: One. Binary fission is a method of ASEXUAL reproduction, so only a single parent is involved. In Amoeba the nucleus of one parent cell divides first, the cytoplasm then constricts in the middle, and the cell splits into two nearly equal daughter cells, each of which grows into a new Amoeba. No gametes and no second parent are needed.

stem: A solution of \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) in water is ____________ in colour.
solution: Blue. Copper sulphate is an ionic compound. When it dissolves in water it furnishes hydrated copper(II) ions, \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), and it is this hydrated \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) ion that gives the solution its characteristic blue colour. (Anhydrous \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) is a white powder; it turns blue as soon as water is added.)

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Raisins are formed by drying grapes. The process that takes place during formation of raisins from grapes is ____________ .
solution: Dehydration. Grapes are dried in the sun so that the water present in them evaporates and is lost. The removal of water from a substance is called dehydration, and the dried grapes so obtained are raisins. (Osmosis is the REVERSE experiment — when dry raisins are kept in water they swell up because water enters them by osmosis.)

stem: Ethanoic acid has a ____________ odour.
solution: Pungent. Ethanoic acid (acetic acid, \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)) is a colourless liquid with a sharp, pungent smell and a sour taste. AMBIGUITY NOTE: a 5-8% aqueous solution of ethanoic acid is vinegar, so option (C) 'Vinegar-like' also describes the same smell and is arguably correct; the answer keyed here, (B) Pungent, is the standard textbook wording and is the option marked in the paper's printed solution.

stem: Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary movements.
solution:
Differences between voluntary and involuntary movements:

| Voluntary movements | Involuntary movements |
|---|---|
| They take place according to our will (they are willed movements). | They are not according to our will; they take place on their own. |
| They are initiated by the cerebrum and controlled (co-ordinated) by the cerebellum. | They are controlled by the medulla oblongata and a part of the midbrain. |
| They are under the control of the central and peripheral nervous systems. | They are under the control of the autonomic nervous system. |
| They occur only when needed and can be started or stopped at will. | They occur continuously throughout life and cannot be stopped at will. |
| Examples: eating, walking, writing, reading. | Examples: breathing, heartbeat, peristalsis (digestion). |

stem: What is the peculiarity of the 'DNA' structure?
solution:
Peculiarities of the structure of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid):
1. DNA is a long double-helical molecule — two polynucleotide strands coiled round each other like a twisted ladder.
2. Its building blocks are nucleotides. Each nucleotide is made of three parts: a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphoric acid (phosphate) group and a nitrogenous base.
3. There are four nitrogenous bases: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) and guanine (G). The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs — A always pairs with T and C always pairs with G.
4. A particular sequence of nucleotides on the DNA molecule constitutes a gene; genes are thus located on the DNA.
5. Each gene is responsible for the synthesis of a particular protein, and therefore for a particular characteristic of the organism.
6. A change (mutation) in a gene can alter the characteristics of the organism, and DNA can replicate itself so that characters are transmitted from parents to offspring.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Draw a well-labelled diagram of longitudinal section of a flower.
solution:
Draw a vertical (longitudinal) section of a typical bisexual flower and label the following parts, from the base upwards:
1. Stalk (pedicel) — the stem that bears the flower.
2. Thalamus and Sepal (calyx) — the outermost green whorl protecting the bud.
3. Petal (corolla) — the coloured whorl that attracts insects for pollination.
4. Stamen (the male reproductive organ, androecium), shown with its two parts: the Filament (the stalk) and the Anther (the swollen top that produces pollen grains).
5. Pistil / Carpel (the female reproductive organ, gynoecium), shown with its three parts from top to bottom: the Stigma (the sticky tip that receives pollen), the Style (the tube connecting stigma to ovary) and the Ovary (the swollen base containing the ovules).
The diagram must be neat, drawn in pencil, with straight label lines that do not cross one another, and titled 'Longitudinal section of a flower'.

stem: Give scientific reason: Roots of plants grow away from light.
solution:
The growth movement of a plant part in response to the direction of a stimulus is called a tropic movement (tropism).
1. The root system responds to the stimulus of gravity and of water: it shows POSITIVE geotropism (it grows downwards, in the direction of gravity) and positive hydrotropism (it grows towards water).
2. With respect to light the root shows NEGATIVE phototropism — the shoot bends towards light, but the root bends away from it.
3. This is useful to the plant, because by growing downwards and away from light the roots penetrate deep into the soil, where they can absorb water and mineral nutrients and can firmly anchor the plant.
Hence the roots of plants grow away from light.

stem: Write any two measures to conserve water.
solution:
Any two of the following measures to conserve water:
1. Close the taps when they are not in use, and repair leaking taps and pipes immediately so that water is not wasted.
2. Practise rainwater harvesting — collect rooftop rainwater and recharge it into wells or store it for use.
3. Recycle and reuse waste water (for example, water used for washing vegetables can be used to water plants).
4. Use drip irrigation or sprinklers instead of flood irrigation in farming.
5. Create public awareness about the importance of water and avoid appliances that need excessive water.

stem: What are fossils?
solution:
Fossils are the preserved remains, impressions or traces of plants, animals and other organisms that lived in the remote past and have been buried and preserved in the layers of the earth's crust (rocks and soil).
1. They are found at different levels or depths of the soil and rock strata; the deeper the layer, the older the fossil.
2. Their age can be estimated from the depth at which they are found and by radioactive carbon dating.
3. The study of fossils (palaeontology) tells us about the structure, age and evolutionary history of extinct organisms, and shows how simpler forms gradually gave rise to more complex ones.
Hence fossils are regarded as important palaeontological evidence for evolution. (Examples: Archaeopteryx, the fossils of ammonites and trilobites.)

stem: What is an alloy? Give two examples with their chemical composition.
solution:
An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of one or more metals with certain non-metallic elements, prepared by melting the constituents together and cooling the melt. Alloys are made to improve properties such as hardness, strength and resistance to corrosion.

Two examples with their composition:

| Name of the alloy | Composition |
|---|---|
| Duralumin | Aluminium + Copper + Magnesium + Manganese \(\mathrm{(Al + Cu + Mg + Mn)}\) |
| Brass | Copper + Zinc \(\mathrm{(Cu + Zn)}\) |

(Other acceptable examples: bronze = \(\mathrm{Cu + Sn}\); stainless steel = \(\mathrm{Fe + Cr + Ni + C}\); solder = \(\mathrm{Pb + Sn}\).)

stem: How is sex determined in human beings?
solution:
Determination of sex in human beings:
1. A human being has 23 pairs (46) of chromosomes — 22 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes. The male has 44 autosomes plus the heteromorphic pair XY, and the female has 44 autosomes plus the homomorphic pair XX.
2. During gamete formation meiosis occurs, so each gamete gets only half the number of chromosomes, i.e. 22 autosomes and one sex chromosome.
3. Therefore the father produces two kinds of sperms — \(22 + X\) and \(22 + Y\) — in equal numbers, while the mother produces only one kind of egg, \(22 + X\).
4. At fertilisation the sex of the child is decided by the sperm:
   - If an \(X\)-bearing sperm fuses with the \(X\)-bearing egg, the zygote is \(44 + XX\) and the child is a GIRL.
   - If a \(Y\)-bearing sperm fuses with the \(X\)-bearing egg, the zygote is \(44 + XY\) and the child is a BOY.
5. Since the two kinds of sperm are produced in equal numbers, the chance of a son and of a daughter is 50% each. Thus the sex of the child is determined by the FATHER (by the sex chromosome carried by the sperm) and not by the mother.

stem: State the different types of neurons. Explain their functions.
solution:
A neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. There are three types of neurons:
1. Sensory (afferent) neurons — they conduct nerve impulses from the sense organs and receptors (skin, eye, ear, nose, tongue) TO the brain and the spinal cord.
2. Motor (efferent) neurons — they carry nerve impulses FROM the brain and the spinal cord to the effector organs, i.e. the muscles and glands, which then respond.
3. Association (relay or inter-) neurons — they lie within the brain and spinal cord and connect the sensory neurons with the motor neurons, integrating and co-ordinating their functions (as in a reflex arc).

stem: What is '3R' mantra? Write its significance.
solution:
The '3R mantra' stands for REDUCE, REUSE and RECYCLE — an effective approach to eliminate waste and conserve natural resources.
1. Reduce — use fewer resources and cut down consumption, e.g. use less paper and avoid plastic carry bags, switch off lights and taps when not needed.
2. Reuse — use an article again instead of throwing it away after a single use, e.g. plastic jars can be reused for storing grains and salt, and old clothes can be reused as dusters.
3. Recycle — send used materials back into a process so that new articles are made from them, e.g. waste plastic, glass, paper and metal are sent to industries and converted into new useful products such as lampshades and handbags.

Significance: all three processes cut down the quantity of raw material and the energy needed to manufacture new articles, reduce the volume of waste and the pollution created during manufacture and disposal, and thus conserve natural resources for future generations.

stem: Metal A has electronic configuration \((2, 8, 1)\) and metal B has \((2, 8, 8, 2)\). Which is more reactive? Why? Identify these metals.
solution:
Metal A is more reactive than metal B.

Reason: The reactivity of a metal depends on how easily it loses its valence electrons to form a positive ion. Metal A has only ONE electron in its outermost shell, so it can lose that single electron very easily to attain a stable octet. Metal B has TWO electrons in its outermost shell and must lose both, which needs more energy. Hence A loses electrons more readily and is the more reactive metal.

Identification: Total electrons in A \(= 2 + 8 + 1 = 11\), so its atomic number is 11 — metal A is SODIUM \(\mathrm{(Na)}\). Total electrons in B \(= 2 + 8 + 8 + 2 = 20\), so its atomic number is 20 — metal B is CALCIUM \(\mathrm{(Ca)}\).

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Explain the disadvantages of a large family size.
solution:
A large family size adversely affects both individual life and community life. Its main disadvantages are:
1. Economic pressure — the earning members have to support many dependants, so the per-head income falls and the family cannot meet even its basic needs.
2. Mother's poor health — repeated pregnancies and childbirth within short intervals weaken the mother and lead to anaemia and other illnesses.
3. Poor housing — the same small dwelling has to accommodate many people, causing overcrowding and unhygienic living conditions.
4. Neglect of children — parents cannot give individual attention, care and affection to each child.
5. Malnutrition — the available food has to be shared among many, so the children do not get a balanced diet and become undernourished.
6. Lack of educational facilities — the family cannot afford good education for all the children, so some are deprived of schooling.
7. Insufficient medical care — timely and adequate medical treatment cannot be provided to every member.
At the community level a large family size increases the population, which increases unemployment and the pressure on land, water and other natural resources. Hence a small family is a happy and healthy family.

Given below are the end products of different reactions involving glucose. Write the reaction number in front of the following:
(i) Anaerobic reaction =
(ii) Reaction in the human muscles =
(iii) Aerobic respiration =
(iv) Reaction in the plant cells =
(v) Reaction in the liver =
solution:
In the given chart glucose is at the centre and the five numbered arrows lead to: \(1 \rightarrow\) Starch, \(2 \rightarrow\) Glycogen, \(3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2 + H_2O}\), \(4 \rightarrow\) Lactic acid, \(5 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2}\) + Ethanol.

(i) Anaerobic reaction = 5. Glucose breaks down without oxygen (alcoholic fermentation, as in yeast) to give ethanol and carbon dioxide.
(ii) Reaction in the human muscles = 4. During vigorous exercise the oxygen supply to the muscles falls short, so glucose is broken down anaerobically to lactic acid, which causes muscle cramps.
(iii) Aerobic respiration = 3. In the presence of oxygen glucose is completely oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, releasing the maximum energy.
(iv) Reaction in the plant cells = 1. Excess glucose produced in photosynthesis is converted into starch and stored in the plant.
(v) Reaction in the liver = 2. Excess glucose in the human body is converted into glycogen and stored in the liver (and in the muscles).

Note: reactions 4 and 5 are BOTH anaerobic; item (i) refers to the fermentation pathway (5) because the muscle pathway (4) is asked separately in item (ii).

stem: What is a homologous series? State any four characteristics of a homologous series.
solution:
A homologous series is a group (series) of organic compounds having a similar structure and similar chemical properties, in which any two successive members differ by one \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) group.

Any four characteristics of a homologous series:
1. Each member differs from the one before it by a \(\mathrm{-CH_2}\) group, i.e. by \(14\) a.m.u. in molecular mass.
2. All the members can be represented by one general formula, e.g. alkanes \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\), alkenes \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\), alkynes \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\).
3. All members contain the same functional group, so they show similar chemical properties. For example, methane and ethane both react with chlorine to give the corresponding chlorides: \(\mathrm{CH_4 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_3Cl + HCl}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_6 + Cl_2 \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl + HCl}\).
4. The physical properties (melting point, boiling point, density, solubility) show a regular gradation as the molecular mass increases along the series.
5. All the members can be prepared by the same general method of preparation, e.g. alcohols can be prepared from the corresponding alkyl halides: \(\mathrm{CH_3Br + KOH \rightarrow CH_3OH + KBr}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Br + KOH \rightarrow C_2H_5OH + KBr}\) (on boiling with aqueous KOH).
